cards.title: The layering rule
items: Nothing links upward, so each library compiles against the ones below it and knows nothing of the ones above.
ToyFrontend has no idea MLIR exists. ldd on the unit-test binary lists no MLIR library, and nm finds no mlir:: symbol in libToyFrontend.a.
Upstream ships this as seven executables, ch1 through ch7, where a change to the lexer is a change to seven files.

cards.title: What the dialect is made of
items: Ops.td declares one dialect, one type and twelve operations; mlir-tblgen turns it into the accessors, builders, verifiers, parser and printer.
Canonicalization patterns live with the dialect, not the passes: getCanonicalizationPatterns is an op hook, and putting it elsewhere makes the two archives mutually dependent.
!toy.struct needs a storage class, so registerTypes() lives in the file that defines it.

cards.title: Why the gate is the point
items: The language is unchanged, so our output can be required to match toyc-ch7 byte for byte at every stage.
1,540 programs, six stages, with and without -opt: 18,480 comparisons, 0 unexpected, nothing skipped.
Renaming toy.mul in a mutant makes the sweep fail, which is how the gate is known not to be vacuous.
